plan.title: Whole-blood case-vs-control DE with effect-size testing
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 60-case vs 60-control unpaired human whole-blood cohort (counts.csv: 12,000 genes x 120 samples, raw gene-level integer counts from Salmon; metadata.csv: 120 rows x 2 columns with condition; single batch). The research question has two parts: which genes differ, and which differences are large enough to matter. With 60 samples per group the cohort is a population-scale sample, and rule R-0015@65aa flags that negative-binomial count models (DESeq2/edgeR) inflate false positives on such cohorts — so the primary test is limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model (TMM normalization, filterByExpr pre-filter, robust eBayes), and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test on log2-CPM serves as the control the rule requires. The 'large enough to matter' part is answered by testing the fold-change threshold inside the model with limma treat (R-0037@e6d8) at |log2FC| >= 1 (2-fold, primary) and 0.58 (1.5-fold, sensitivity), rather than post-hoc filtering on the estimate. The report carries effect size beside every p-value (R-0089@69f0) and the population-cohort caution. Sample-structure QC precedes the model (blind vst, PCA, distance heatmap). Two limitations are stated up front: the matrix is gene-level counts only, so tximport transcript-length offsets (R-0018@a472) cannot be applied and differential-transcript-usage bias cannot be corrected; and the metadata holds only condition, so no covariates or batch structure can be modeled.

Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with p-value histogram inspection before adjustment
